title: Sequence-controlled switchover for staggered tenant fallback
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Customers experienced cascading errors during a partial cross-region degradation that affected both Hosted and Dedicated tenants. The immediate root cause was a race between routing rehoming and KV-cache lease expiry that produced inconsistent model state for a subset of tenant sessions. Goal: produce an operator-safe, sequence-controlled switchover playbook that can be executed by SRE/Support to move tenants off a degrading region in a prioritized, staggered fashion to avoid global cache storms and tail-latency spikes. This ticket covers the runbook, CLI helpers, temporary gating flags to be used during incidents, and a small bugfix for the KV-lease-renewal logic that surfaced during the incident.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook verified in staging with a simulated region slowdown: sequence control works and max p95 latency increase < 15% for remaining region
A CLI helper (switchover-orchestrator) exists and is documented in the runbook with examples for hosted + dedicated tenants
KV-lease-renewal bugfix merged and deployed to canary; no lease double-release observed during test scenarios
Support playbook contains tenant-priority buckets and rollback steps; on-call has run tabletop exercise
Post-mitigation dashboards (per-tenant error-rate, rehome-rate, KV-miss rate) created and wired into incident template
runbook_steps: 1) Signal: Confirm alerts triggered: region_load > 85% for > 5m AND p50/p95 error-rate increase for model serving routes
2) Classify: Query affected-tenants endpoint to split tenants into emergency/high/standard buckets using tenant SLA and active sessions
3) Throttle: Apply soft-throttle on new session admits to the degraded region (kinetic rate-limiter 'soft-admit') to stop new long-running sessions from starting

4) Drain-Stagger: For each priority bucket (emergency -> high -> standard) do: a) mark tenant routing state to draining, b) set tenant-specific rehome-window = Xs (configurable), c) perform graceful connection-mark and allow active KV prefixes to expire on natural access or be cached in destination before rehome

5) Controlled-Route-Shift: Use switchover-orchestrator CLI to shift traffic in small shards (default shard-size=5% of tenant concurrency) with 30s observation windows between shards and automatic rollback on >5% error-rate regression
6) KV-Consistency-Safety: Before shifting a shard, issue KV prefetch for hot prefixes, set temporary KV-ttl-extension flag for the shard to avoid lease expiry during migration
7) Fallback: If destination region shows p95 latency increase > 20% within observation window, stop further shards, revert current shard, and open hypothesis channel for manual triage
8) Finalize: Once all shards moved for a tenant, clear temporary flags, run tenant-level verification job, and mark routing state as normal
9) Rollback plan: Outline exact commands to roll back last N shards and where to look for telemetry to validate rollback succeeded
decisions: Use sequence-controlled shard switchover instead of whole-tenant atomic rehome to avoid synchronized KV lease churn
Prioritize tenants using SLA + active-session count; customers with Dedicated pools are put in a higher-priority bucket by default
Implement short-lived KV-ttl-extension per-shard (config flag) rather than changing global cache mechanics — faster to ship and safer for canary
Expose a single op-facing CLI (switchover-orchestrator) instead of multiple ad-hoc scripts to reduce human error during outages
